note: 80-industry.json is the source of the shared utility nodes (facility.water, facility.electricity, facility.nitrogen, facility.argon, facility.helium, facility.gases, facility.gases.oxygen, facility.steam, facility.compressed-air, facility.coal, facility.oil, facility.steam.soda-ash, facility.water.coconut-shell, facility.water.uv-lamp). No id in this fragment was changed, renamed or deleted; all 20 ids that other fragments reference still resolve. What this pass did. DISSOLVED one routing point: facility.power.generation, whose five plant children now hang directly off facility.power and whose 1980/1990 Taiwan mix facts moved up into that node. FOLDED 12 bare processes into their parents' descriptions, numbers kept in facts, so this fragment now has zero R5 bare-process leaves (it had 35). RETYPED 22 nodes to kind note (it had none): the people/wages/design-history leaves, the RCRA regime, the electricity tariff, the helium shortage, the three 'where did the gas go' leaves, the fab-cost and fab-workforce figures, and the two foundries stories. RECATEGORISED 83 nodes out of energy, which CHECKLIST section 3 reserves for generation and the grid and only for kind facility and process - 69 went to industry (heavy equipment, mining, and the extractive commodities) and 14 to power (transformers, switchboards, contactors, busbar, insulators, alternators, motors); energy is now 28 nodes, all facility or process, down from 119. SPLIT facility.hazardous-waste.generation from a question-framed leaf into a material with three real waste-stream children. ADDED 4 nodes (three waste streams, the commercial shipping documents). DELETED 18: 12 folded bare processes, the dissolved routing point, and five internal duplicates after re-pointing every reference inside this file (facility.gases.nitrogen-purge-system, facility.water.leach-plant-water, facility.steam.limestone, logistics.people.hk-headcount, logistics.people.wage-index). Node count 305 -> 291; audit WARNs 249 -> 34. No other fragment was touched and no id changed. Three AUDIT FAILs remain and all three are the same non-defect: a trunk or branch root holding its own canonical raw-material node with `children`, which is the only thing that makes it reachable (industry -> facility.water, chem -> chem.natural-gas, chem.crude.reservoir.oil-column -> chem.petroleum). See edge_fixes. Zero R2/R3/R5/R6/R7 findings remain in this fragment; the 34 WARNs are all R4 duplicate-name or relative-name, and the duplicates are all cross-fragment and proposed below.

edge_fixes.why: Resolved while I worked - listed so you can see it was not ignored. CHECKLIST 1a: these were `children` edges into MY utility nodes from other fragments, each dragging a 25-40 node water or electricity subtree into a supply line that has no business containing a water treatment plant or a switchboard. All 18 water edges and all 33 electricity edges are now `from`. Nothing left to do here.

Not my nodes at all, and not a real defect: chem.natural-gas and chem.petroleum are the canonical shared crude and gas nodes and audit.mjs flags them by name, but their remaining `children` parents live in 70-petrochem.json. chem is the trunk that OWNS chem.natural-gas, exactly as industry owns facility.water, and audit.mjs whitelists c64.bottoms-out / facility.power / facility.water but not the petrochemical trunk `chem`. One line in the whitelist fixes both.

One edge in my own file, left deliberately, and it is the last one standing on facility.water. `industry` is the branch that owns facility.water - it is the only parent of it anywhere in the tree - and a utility root has to hang off something. audit.mjs whitelists c64.bottoms-out, facility.power and facility.water as legitimate owners, which was written for a different spine layout; it does not whitelist a branch root like `industry` (or `chem`, above). Moving or renaming the node to dodge that whitelist would hide the defect rather than fix it, so it stands. The one-line fix is in scripts/audit.mjs, which I do not own: add `p === 'industry' && id === 'facility.water'` to the owned list on line 62, or add 'industry' to the whitelist generally.

merges.why: same thing, two copies. This fragment's node is the whole plant - pretreatment, ion exchange, mixed bed, RO, UV, the distribution loop - and has the era-specific 10-15 MOhm-cm / 60-80 C loop practice; the other is a bare leaf. The other file's good detail (18.2 MOhm-cm at 25 C, TOC below 5 ppb, the ozone polish) is modern practice and belongs in the survivor's note.
same substance. Atmospheric air is the terminal raw input of the whole bulk-gas chain and belongs in one place; the composition facts are duplicated in both descriptions.
same operation, described twice. This fragment's node carries the desulphurisation target (<0.5 ppm S), the 3:1 steam ratio, the 800-850 C / 15-25 bar conditions and the shift step.
same substance, and 60-metals publishes the canonical node. Merge this one and facility.compressed-air.caustic-soda together.

CHECKLIST 1b. Both describe chlor-alkali NaOH at 3-4 V cell voltage and 2200-2500 kWh/t; the metals node is the canonical one and already carries the membrane-cell story. My file's own references to it can be re-made by hand without breaking anything.

same ore. This fragment's facility.compressed-air.fluorspar (the fluorspar that feeds the HF for CFCs) and its mine should fold into the metals fragment's metal.fluorspar node and its children rather than carrying a second copy of the vein and the mine.
same ore; this fragment's node is the more general one and already carries the Bushveld / Oman / Kola places and the mine beneath it.
same ore. The general 'Iron ore (hematite/magnetite)' node belongs in one place; it is currently the blast-furnace feed for the power station's turbine steel, which is exactly the general case.
same material; this fragment's node is the general 'Metallurgical coke' and carries the coking-coal seam.
same material; third copy of metallurgical coke.

same monomer. Three copies survive now (facility.steam.styrene, peripheral.tv.cabinet.abs.styrene, c64.case.abs-resin.styrene); the general one should survive. If the 40-chassis or 90-peripherals node turns out to be the richer one, keep that instead and re-point the divinylbenzene sibling edge.
same substance, and 60-metals publishes the canonical Solvay-process node with a fuller description; this fragment's lime-soda branch should point at it.
same facility; 60-metals already has the quarry node and the carbonate bed under it.
same substance. metal.sulphuric-acid is the canonical 93-99% contact-process node; this fragment's copy exists only to hang the recovered-sulphur node off it, and that edge can be re-made directly.
same element. chem.sulfur is the canonical brimstone node; the recovered-sulphur history (post-1970 Claus, displacing Frasch) belongs in its note.

second bauxite quarry in the tree for the same purpose. Both this node and facility.power.bauxite-mine sit inside the water/alum and the ACSR/alumina branches; metal.bauxite and metal.bauxite.mine are the canonical pair.

the Bayer process is already written in the metals fragment (metal.bayer.digestion, metal.red-mud, metal.bauxite.beneficiation). This fragment's copy should become a `from` edge on the aluminium conductor rather than a second subtree.
same substance. metal.salt-brine already has the solar-salt pan and the halite rock beneath it, which is exactly what this fragment's node and its rock-salt mine inline.
same substance. chem.solvents.cfc has the full synthesis chain (methane chlorination -> chloroform -> CFC) and this fragment's fluorspar/HF chain duplicates it.

fixes_conflicts.wanted: note (or just remove the entry and let the fragment stand)
fixes_conflicts.why: I have set this node to kind note in 80-industry.json because CHECKLIST section 2 says a statement about the industry is a note, and because its sibling logistics.people.c64-system-team - the same kind of thing, four people in five weeks - is a note. The curated fixes table retypes it back to facility at build time (the log line reads 'retyped note -> facility'), and it would then disagree with its sibling. CHECKLIST section 0 says to write down why in the note, which I have done. One-line change in a file I do not own.

left_alone.why: see fixes_conflicts. The fragment says note, the build says facility, and the audit is clean either way because category industry imposes no kind restriction.

name kept verbatim although it reads as relative. audit.mjs identifies cross-cutting services by exact name ('Ultrapure water for the fab', 'Ordinary industrial water', 'Water for a factory', 'Electricity at the factory wall'); renaming would remove the node from the R1a check without fixing anything. The id is what other fragments reference and it is unchanged.

the duplicate-name warning against mb.logic.cmos...locos.nitride.ammonia.hydrogen is a false positive: this node is the bulk merchant gas supply, the other is hydrogen as a reactant inside a named process. Left alone deliberately.

a genuine duplicate of the shared chem.natural-gas, but merging it would mean deleting an id inside my own file on the strength of a proposal I have not applied - and CHECKLIST 1b says link, never retype, in both directions. I have re-pointed my own two internal references (the helium cryo-separation and the hydrogen reformer) at chem.natural-gas so that the duplicate is now a leaf holding only LNG, North Sea and US-domestic sourcing detail; deleting it is a one-line follow-up once the coordinator agrees the survivor.

retyped to note rather than folded into facility.power. The two-part tariff and the demand charge are the reason an electronics factory's power bill behaved the way it did; keeping it as a note preserves the sourced 7.0 c/kWh figure without pretending a tariff is a thing in the supply chain.

kept as part, not note. A manifest is a physical multi-part carbonless form that travelled with the load and could be weighed; only its category moved (logistics -> packaging, since CAT_OK.logistics accepts only process and facility).

kept as a note with its facts rather than folded. The Dougherty breakdown is the most-cited contemporaneous cost estimate in the whole story and it is the only place the eight DRAMs' $14.80 appears; folding it into the branch description would lose the itemisation.
